issues.description: Inner contradiction in the problem statement about the type used to store animals in Farm: the UML diagram (and earlier textual UML lines) declares the attribute as animals: List<Animal>, but the Part 3 textual instructions explicitly require using a Set implemented with a HashSet to ensure uniqueness. This conflicting guidance can confuse students about which collection type to implement and which properties (e.g., uniqueness) are required.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the problem statement consistent: either update the UML and earlier references to show animals: Set<Animal> (and mention HashSet in the text), or change the Part 3 textual instruction to require a List/ArrayList. Prefer explicitly specifying Set<Animal> / HashSet in both UML and text if uniqueness is pedagogically intended.

issues.description: Cross-artifact structural mismatch: Part 3 of the problem statement requires the Farm to use a Set (HashSet) for the animals attribute to enforce uniqueness, but the reference solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This makes the solution inconsistent with the stated requirement and can prevent students from using the intended data structure or cause test failures if tests check for Set semantics.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution (and template examples) with the problem statement: change the Farm implementation to use a Set<Animal> and initialize it as a new HashSet<>() in the no-argument constructor. Update any methods that rely on List-specific behavior (if any) to work with Set. Alternatively, if List semantics were intended, update the Part 3 text to require a List (and update the instruction about uniqueness accordingly). Ensure UML, textual instructions, template stubs, and the solution all use the same collection type.
